Compute an exact locator polynomial in a skew-polynomial ring.

Let L = GF(2^256) = GF(2)[z]/(P(z)), where P is the monic irreducible binary polynomial encoded by 0x10000000000000000000000000000000000000000000200000040000080000001. Bit i of this integer is the coefficient of z^i. Field addition is bitwise XOR; field multiplication is carryless polynomial multiplication reduced modulo P. Every field element below is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits in this polynomial basis (no 0x prefix).

Define sigma(u)=u^(2^32). In the Ore ring L[x;sigma], coefficients are written on the left and x*u=sigma(u)*x. For b in L, define N_0(b)=1 and N_j(b)=b*sigma(b)*...*sigma^(j-1)(b). The right evaluation of f(x)=sum_j f_j*x^j at b is f[b]=sum_j f_j*N_j(b). Thus b is a right root exactly when f[b]=0.

The following 8 nonzero points are promised to be left P-independent: equivalently, the square matrix with entry N_j(b_i) in row j=0,...,n-1 and column i=1,...,n is nonsingular over L. They are also promised to lie in one sigma-conjugacy class, where b and b' are conjugate when b'=sigma(c)*b*c^(-1) for some nonzero c.

Compute an exact locator polynomial in a skew-polynomial ring.

Let L = GF(2^256) = GF(2)[z]/(P(z)), where P is the monic irreducible binary polynomial encoded by 0x10000000000000000000000000000000000000000000200000040000080000001. Bit i of this integer is the coefficient of z^i. Field addition is bitwise XOR; field multiplication is carryless polynomial multiplication reduced modulo P. Every field element below is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits in this polynomial basis (no 0x prefix).

Define sigma(u)=u^(2^32). In the Ore ring L[x;sigma], coefficients are written on the left and x*u=sigma(u)*x. For b in L, define N_0(b)=1 and N_j(b)=b*sigma(b)*...*sigma^(j-1)(b). The right evaluation of f(x)=sum_j f_j*x^j at b is f[b]=sum_j f_j*N_j(b). Thus b is a right root exactly when f[b]=0.

The following 8 nonzero points are promised to be left P-independent: equivalently, the square matrix with entry N_j(b_i) in row j=0,...,n-1 and column i=1,...,n is nonsingular over L. They are also promised to lie in one sigma-conjugacy class, where b and b' are conjugate when b'=sigma(c)*b*c^(-1) for some nonzero c.
